You end up paying $95 for the Ascend in exchange for 150K Hilton points. For the Aspire’s $450 fee, you get the same 150K Hilton points, $500 in airline credits ($750 if you time your application right), $250 in resort credit (which can be used for room rates), a free weekend night at any Hilton in the world, top-tier Hilton Diamond status and of course the standard slew of benefits you’d expect from a premium card (TSA credit, etc.). I think the Aspire may be one of the most overvalued cards right now, and I’d be shocked if Amex doesn’t devalue it in the next year or so.

The days of App-O-rama are more a thing of the past. I think that it is a balanced list, as you don’t necessarily want to add multiple cards at once, depending on how new you are to the game, I know that my consideration list is far from static. If I could redo something’s I would have taken it a lot slower at the beginning ( I don’t think I would have applied for Chase Amazon Prime card so early in the game, I also would have gone with a different strategy. I would have rather had the Ritz card and might have Double dipped the CSP/CSR). I would have done a ton more research at the beginning and gone with a different strategy – This list is always changing and some of the best card deals don’t always hang around that long. Also I would have planned out a P#2 strategy from the start.

Yet even this list is YMMV, for any number of reason’s both for Personal/Business cards, as well as your average account age, length and depth of credit history, overall debt utilization, FICO’s , number of Inquiries. So while a Tier 2 or Minor league card offerings, I will say that this a great tool – but you still need to analyze for your goals and personal situation. There is a reddit Flowchart that is a great reference tool that gives suggestions for Cash back cards, Miles/points cards for travel and recommendations. At this point your normally best waiting for an awesome sign-up bonus to come along rather than slotting a 2nd tier card in a 5/24 slot.

JMHO
